label: Phase 1 tank hits and raid pulses, scaled so gear separates
summary: One healer's share of a Phase 1 raid fight, scaled up until the strongest raid-ready healer covers about 80 percent of what comes in and the weakest about 60: a tank taking big melee hits, raid-wide damage in regular pulses, and four more raid members to look after, with the healer taking its share of the raid-wide damage.
notes: A healing sim ranks gear under a stated incoming-damage profile. It never says one healer class beats another, and every healer number the site publishes names this profile. No client table states a creature's damage, so every figure below is a stated assumption, and this profile is a stand-in for Phase 1 that is NOT a named boss. It was first sized to an Onyxia-class boss, but at that size the raid-ready healers covered 80 to 97 percent of what came in, healing met the damage, and more healing power changed nothing, so gear tied. The retune rule (design/reviews/2026-10-08-heal-profile-retune.md) is: scale the tank hit size and the raid-wide pulse damage together, keeping their ratio and cadence, by the smallest multiplier at which the strongest raid-ready healer covers about 80 percent of the incoming damage, the weakest about 60, every bare set (no raid consumables) covers less than half, and mana is a live constraint (a bare set's mana runs out before the fight ends for every healer, and a raid set's for at least one). The multiplier chosen was 1.5 on 2026-10-08 and is 1.65 since 2026-11-01: client 1.60.1.70707 gave the Restoration druid Bloom and let heals over time crit (the client flags every trained heal over time PERIODIC_CAN_CRIT, and Blizzard's beta notes of 24 September say so for Rejuvenation), which took the druid to 91 percent at 1.5, and 1.65 is the smallest multiplier that brings every raid set back between about 60 and 85 percent (design/reviews/2026-11-01-sim-audit-round4/hybrids.md). It is 1.85 since 2026-11-02: round 7's engine fixes (Mana Spring stacking with Blessing of Wisdom, Healing Stream counted in the shaman's healing, Oath of Light, Water Shield on raid damage, casts pushed back by the pulses) took the Restoration shaman to 97 percent at 1.65, and 1.85 is the smallest multiplier that brings every raid set back between about 60 and 85 percent on the published gear (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round7/healers.md). The next retune (Phase 2 gear) follows the same rule. The figures are damage AFTER mitigation, because the fake raid has no armor or avoidance to roll. They are the share of the fight one healer is asked to cover, not the whole raid's incoming damage, and they stay the same for every spec and every gear set so the ranking compares gear and not fights. Every figure above is the level-60 band's. Below 60 each leveling band fights the same fight at its own level, with the damage its own content deals (bands, below): until 2026-11-03 every band fought the level-60 figures, so a level-20 healer covered a few percent of a raid fight and every rank choice below 60 was a healing-per-mana figure.

tuning.reason: The tank hit and the raid pulse are the Onyxia-class figures first assumed (1,150 and 300) times one multiplier, set by the retune rule: 1.5 on 2026-10-08, 1.65 on 2026-11-01 once the client let heals over time crit, 1.85 on 2026-11-02 once the engine fixes of round 7 (Mana Spring stacking with Blessing of Wisdom, Healing Stream counted, Oath of Light, Water Shield on raid damage) took the strongest raid set to 97 percent. The multiplier is a tuning, not a measured boss, so the two answers are its bounds: /tiers/healer orders two healers only when the order holds, and the gap is beyond the error, at both.

tank.reason: A raid tank has about 9,500 health in Phase 1 gear with raid buffs. The hit is a stand-in sized by the retune rule, not a boss's: 1.85 times the 1,150 an Onyxia-class boss was first assumed to land on a mitigated tank, which is the smallest scale at which the five healers' raid-ready sets cover between about 60 and 85 percent of the incoming damage and bare sets less than half. With misses, dodges and parries averaged in one hit lands about every 3.3 seconds, about 645 damage a second; each hit rolls 25 percent either side.

members.reason: A raid member that is not the tank has about 5,000 health: a plate or mail wearer sits above it and a cloth wearer below.

pulse.reason: Raid-wide damage in regular pulses (a breath, a wing buffet, a periodic shadow bolt volley): every five seconds three of the five members of the healer's group, the healer among them, take 555, about 333 damage a second spread over the group the healer stands in. The healer is one of the five because raid-wide damage does not skip the player casting the heals; until round 6 (design/reviews/2026-11-02-sim-audit-round6/healers.md) it landed only on the four others, so every group heal put a fifth of its healing on a healer who was never hurt. The total is unchanged: three members a pulse, now chosen from five. Scaled by the same 1.85 as the tank hit, so the tank-to-raid ratio and the cadence are what they were.

bands.rule: Below 60 each band fights the same fight at its own level (owner ruling, sim-accuracy round 10): the same length, cadence, spread and members, with the damage its own content deals and the health a character of the band has. A band's content is the open dungeons whose last boss stands from the band's level to five levels above it, the dungeons a group of that level goes to; at 60 it is the open raid, because the level-60 profile is a raid fight. A last boss's damage a second is its melee plus its spells. Its melee is its creature_template hit, melee attack power over 14 plus the mean of its minimum and maximum melee damage times its damage multiplier, over its attack time (cmangos Creature::UpdateDamagePhysical), less the share of the fight it spends casting or channelling. Its spells are every damaging spell its AI casts while it is tanked (the spell list its template names, else its EventAI rows, else its script, at the melee-range timers; at 60, Onyxia's ground phase), each counted once a cast on one target: the cast's mean damage at the boss's level (cmangos spell_template, the 1.12 values: base points, dice and points per level; ticks of a periodic aura over its duration; a weapon-damage effect as one melee hit plus its bonus; triggered spells as they trigger) over the mean of its repeat timer. Heals, buffs, summons, crowd control without damage and one-off health-threshold casts are left out. A band's damage is the median of its last bosses' damage a second times the content's client damage modifier, and the tank hit and the raid pulse both scale by that against the reference band's, so the tank-to-raid ratio stays what it is at 60. The tank's and the members' health scale by the client's expected player health at the band's level against level 60's. The tuning scale multiplies every band alike, so a band keeps its place inside the tuning bounds. A level between two bands fights the band at or below it, the way rank choices run from one band to the next, and a level below 20 fights band 20. Each row states its derived figures, and loading refuses a row whose figures are not the rule's. Pulls (owner ruling, sim-accuracy round 11): a dungeon is mostly trash, and a hard trash pull often hits harder than the last boss. A band's trash is every creature its dungeons spawn that is hostile to players (client FactionTemplate) and can be fought, less its bosses (instance_encounters), vendors, critters and hidden triggers; a spawn with a random entry stands for its first listed one (creature_spawn_entry, else spawn_group_entry). It is cut into pulls the way the server pulls: a pulled creature calls every creature of its own faction within its assistance radius, and each of those calls the next (mangos-classic Creature::MarkCallAssistanceOnPull), and spawn groups that aggro together and aggro-linked creatures (creature_linking, creature_linking_template) come with them. The radius is the creature's own CallForHelp where creature_template states one, else bands.pull_rule's (10 yards, TrinityCore's CreatureFamilyAssistanceRadius: cmangos ships 5, which pulls most of the Deadmines one mob at a time). Line of sight is not checked. A pull's damage a second is the sum of its mobs', each counted the way a last boss is (melee less its casting share, plus its repeating in-combat spells from creature_spell_list or EventAI, once a cast on one target). Pulls are weighted by the mobs in them, because a run spends its time killing mobs, and the band fights the pull at bands.pull_rule's percentile (the 75th: a quarter of a run's mobs come in pulls at least this hard). The pull multiplier is that pull's damage a second over the median last boss's, never below 1, so a band fights the harder of the two; the band's damage is its median last boss's times the pull multiplier times the content's damage modifier. A pull's mobs all stand on the tank, so the trash's melee and aimed spells are the tank's; the tank-to-raid ratio is still kept as at 60. Each band row states its dungeons' pull counts, the pull it fights spawn by spawn, and that pull's mobs, and loading refuses a pull whose mobs do not sum to it or a multiplier that is not the rule's.
bands.notes: Client 1.60.1.70707 holds no creature's damage: CreatureDifficulty lists 184 creatures and none of these bosses, and ExpectedStat's creature columns are one generic curve with no line between a dungeon boss and a raid boss (scaling the level-60 raid fight down that curve left a level-20 healer covering about a tenth of the fight and dry inside 30 seconds, the very fault the ruling names). So the bosses' damage is creature_template's (cmangos classic-db, the commit data/pipeline/classic_quest_levels.py pins), their levels are creature_template's and Wowhead's Forever tooltips agree on every one, and the client supplies the rest: ExpectedStat (the Classic set, ExpansionID -2, row id = level) gives PlayerHealth; ContentTuningXExpected rows 3400 to 3428 give every Classic dungeon's content tuning (5237 to 5256, which LFGDungeons names) ExpectedStatMod 489, creature melee and spell damage times 1.2, while the raids' tuning (4509) has none, so the dungeon bands carry 1.2 and the raid 1.0. That modifier is one client table with no Blizzard post behind it. Shadowfang Keep (Archmage Arugal, 26), Blackfathom Deeps (Aku'mai, 28), the Stockade (Bazil Thredd, 29), Scarlet Monastery's Library (Arcanist Doan, 37), Uldaman (Archaedas, 47) and Zul'Farrak (Chief Ukorz Sandscalp, 48) fall between bands under the five-level window; Forever's new dungeons state no boss in either source and are left out. The client stores these bosses' spells only in a scaled form whose formula it does not state (Wowhead's tooltips print no amount for them), so the amounts are spell_template's. Each spell row names the AI source of its timer: cmangos classic-db creature_spell_list and creature_ai_scripts, and the mangos-classic ScriptDevAI scripts boss_herod.cpp, boss_mograine_and_whitemane.cpp, boss_thermaplugg.cpp and boss_onyxia.cpp at commit ff13624. The pulls come from cmangos classic-db's spawns (creature, creature_spawn_entry, spawn_group, spawn_group_spawn, spawn_group_entry, creature_linking, creature_linking_template) and its trash templates and AI (creature_template, creature_spell_list, creature_ai_scripts) at the same commit; client 1.60.1.70707's Creature and CreatureDifficulty hold 184 creatures and none of these dungeons' trash, so the client gives only FactionTemplate (which creatures are hostile). The Scarlet Monastery's four wings share one map and are told apart by position.
